page: Microsoft Azure E20ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadv6 series, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 10 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 microarchitecture incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware instruction support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic operations. GPU hardware is not included.

Memory capacity is configured at 160.0 GB RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive workloads. For scratch space and low-latency disk operations, the instance bundles 1181 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. In benchmark evaluations, the E20ads_v6 shows strong single-core compute performance, ranking in the top 25% with a stress-ng single-core score of 3080.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1962.0. Memory subsystem throughput is similarly marked by a top 25% PassMark memory score of 2775.61, while sustained uncached read bandwidth reaches 76.66 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 55.94 GB/sec.

Multithreaded metrics fall into the middle 50% across general compute benchmarks, including a PassMark CPU score of 32617.89 and Geekbench multi-core score of 12766.0. Redis SET throughput measures 28.5 million operations per second, supported by steady memory throughput and high single-thread execution efficiency. Large-model prompt processing (70B parameters) demonstrates lower throughput at 5.46 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators, making CPU-based inference effective primarily on lightweight models.

By delivering an 8 GB per vCPU density bundled with local high-speed NVMe storage, the instance presents balanced resource efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise deployments. The server is well configured for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise relational database management systems (RDBMS), data warehousing ETL tasks, and memory-constrained analytical pipelines.
